definitions: A type of blood cell produced in the bone marrow and found in the blood. Red blood cells contain a protein called hemoglobin, which carries oxygen from the lungs to all parts of the body.
The most common type of blood cell and the vertebrate's principal means of delivering oxygen (O2) to the body tissues via blood flow through the circulatory system.
examples: Red blood cell production is vital.
Each red blood cell has a function.
A red blood cell count can indicate health issues.
